Course Overview

What is a Data Pipeline?

  • data pipeline is a set of processes that move data from one system to another, including ingestion, transformation and storage.
  • Importance:
    • Automates data processing
    • Improves efficiency
    • Ensures data consistency

Components of a Data Pipeline

  1. Data Sources: APIs, databases, files, streams
  2. Processing: Filtering, aggregating, joining, enriching
  3. Storage: Data warehouses, Data lake
  4. Orchestration & Monitoring: Apache Airflow
  5. Analysis

Important principles:

  • Data Lineage: Trace how data flows and transforms across stages.
  • Governance: Apply policies for access, privacy, and compliance (GDPR).
  • Example: Being able to track how a customer email was collected, processed, and used in reports.

Data Lineage & Governance in Pipelines

Principles of Scalable ETL

Other important principles: Scalability, Data Quality, Automation, Cloud Integration, …

Batch versus Streaming Processing

Batch: Processes data at scheduled intervals

Streaming: Processes data continuously in real-time

Trade-offs:

    • Streaming provides low latency but is more complex
    • Batch is easier to implement but lacks real-time insights

Task: Identify scenarios for batch versus streaming processing

Modern Pipeline Architectures

  • Lambda Architecture
      • Batch layer: processes large historical datasets.
      • Speed layer: handles real-time streams.
      • Use case: Banking (fraud detection + regulatory reports).
  • Kappa Architecture
      • Streaming-first, no batch layer.
      • All data treated as a stream.
      • Simpler design, but requires strong real-time infrastructure.
      • Use case: IoT telemetry or social media analytics.
  • Trend: Many organizations adopt hybrid approaches depending on latency, cost, and complexity.

Data Partitioning Strategies

Data partitioning: Managing datasets efficiently.

  • Horizontal Partitioning: Each partition (shard) contains a subset of rows of the same table (in the same schema), each shard holds different data-> useful for distributing data across multiple servers to improve scalability and performance
  • Vertical Partitioning: Dividing table into smaller tables, containing a subset of columns-> Optimize performance by grouping frequently accessed columns together and storing less frequently accessed columns separately

Other strategies: Range Partitioning, List Partitioning, Hash Partitioning and Composite Partitioning.

Parallel Processing Techniques

Parallel processing is essential in data engineering for handling large datasets efficiently. Here are some techniques:

  • Data parallelism: Involves partitioning data into smaller subsets and performing parallel computations on each subset
  • Task Parallelism: Executing different tasks or threads concurrently. AKA multi-threading -> different processors or cores handle different tasks
  • Pipeline Parallelism: Divides a task into a series of stages, with each stage being processed in parallel. Just like an assembly line, where different stages of a task are processed simultaneously
  • Distributed Computing: Involves distributing tasks across multiple machines in a network. Enables the executing of data processing tasks across a cluster of machines, providing scalability and fault tolerance.

Workflow Orchestration

Involves designing, executing and optimizing workflows to ensure that different tasks and processes work harmoniously. It is not only a simple automation by integrating tasks across different systems but it also ensures they follow a logical sequence.

Tools: Apache Airflow

Pipeline Monitoring & Observability

  • Monitoring: Tracks pipeline health & performance.
    • Metrics: data freshness, throughput, latency.
    • Logs: success & error details for debugging.
    • Alerts: automatic notifications (Slack, email, PagerDuty).
  • Observability: Goes deeper — provides insights into why issues happen.
    • Correlates failures, delays, and anomalies.
  • Example: Detecting late-arriving data in a sales dashboard before it impacts reports.

How does it work?

  • Defining task sequences: Establishing the order in which tasks should be executed
  • Setting Dependencies: Ensuring tasks are executed in the correct order based on their dependencies
  • Integrating Systems: Connecting various systems and applications to enable seamless data flow and task execution
  • Monitoring and Error handling: Continuously monitoring workflows to identify and resolve issues promptly

Why is it important?

  • Ensures efficient data processing
  • Automates repetitive tasks
  • Enhances data reliability and consistency

Example: Automation of ETL processes

Introduction to Airflow

Apache Airflow is an open-source platform for developing, scheduling and monitoring workflows.

Some key features are:

    • Modular architecture
    • Dynamic pipelines (python)
    • Extensible
    • Elegant

Components of Airflow

  • DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs): represent workflows
  • Tasks: Individual units of work within a DAG
  • Operators: Define the nature of tasks (e.g. BashOperator, PythonOperator)
  • Scheduler: responsible for triggering scheduled workflows and submitting tasks to the executor. It reads DAG files to determine what tasks to run and when.
  • Executor: Runs within the scheduler process. It handles the execution of tasks
  • Webserver: Provides user interface to inspect, trigger and debug the behavior of DAGs and tasks. Used for monitoring the status of workflows, tasks and view logs

Schedule interval

Minute|hour|day-of-month|month|day-of-week

Schedule Interval Exercises

  • schedule="0 6 * * 1-5“
    • Every weekday (Monday–Friday) at 06:00
  • schedule="30 2 1 * *“
    • 30 on the first day of every month
  • schedule="0 */4 * * *"
    • Every 4 hours (00:00, 04:00, 08:00, 12:00, 16:00, 20:00)
  • Run the pipeline every 10 minutes between 08:00 and 18:00 every day.
    • */10 8-18 * * *
  • Run the pipeline every 30 minutes on Saturdays and Sundays.
    • */30 * * * 6,0
  • Run the pipeline every hour between 06:00 and 20:00 on weekdays.
    • 20 * * 1-5

Challenges in Data Pipelines

  • Data Quality Issues: Missing, inconsistent or incorrect data
  • Data Integration Complexity: Integrating data from various sources, formats and databases
  • Latency Issues: Ensuring timely data availability
  • Scalability: Handling increasing data volume
  • Monitoring & Troubleshooting: Identifying and resolving pipeline failures

Pipeline Reliability

  • Pipelines should be tested like code.
  • Unit tests for transformations, schema tests, data quality checks.
  • CD for pipelines: Git + automated deployment of DAGs.
  • Example: Spotify runs tests before deploying new ETL DAGs in Airflow.
